messages.author: 7af7a63e6e5f763f
messages.subject: Fasta to Adegenet via DartR
parts:
Hi Everyone,

I realize that this is not a direct dartR question, but since dartR masters so many common genetic conversions in R, I was hoping to get some advice.

My question is, does dartR or any other program have a way of reading multiple fastas and converting to genind/genlight formats while properly converting the ambiguity codes?

It is easy to read genome-scale fastas in R using the apex functions read.multiFASTA() and then multidna2genind() to convert to a genind object. Unfortunately, this relies on DNAbin2genind and seems to take the ambiguity codes for say heterozygous states (e.g., w = A/T) and codes them as NA in the genind object. Of course that is unacceptable for any popgen studies.

If anyone has any suggestions for doing this for a folder of fasta loci, I would be really appreciative. 

Thanks so much!

Frank

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: Fasta to Adegenet via DartR
parts:
Hi Frank,

I wrote a function to convert FASTA files to genlight object (gl.read.fasta). To use this new function you should install the developing version of dartR as shown in the code below.

Please give it a try and let us know your thoughts.

# install the developing version of dartR
library(dartR)
gl.install.vanilla.dartR(flavour = "dev")

library(dartR)
# Folder where the fasta files are located. In this example, files are in the working directory
folder_samples <- getwd()
# listing the FASTA files, including their path. Files have an extension that contains "fas".
file_names <- list.files(path = folder_samples, pattern = "*.fas", full.names = TRUE)
# reading fasta files
gl_list <- gl.read.fasta(file_names)

Cheers,
Luis
